findings.title: Early template variable interpolation breaks detection of $__range and ad-hoc filters
findings.body:
In `runSplitQuery`, `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` is now called before partitioning and before `runShardSplitQuery` delegates sub-requests to `runSplitQuery`. This causes two problems:

1. `querySupportsSplitting` (line 287) checks `!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` so that queries containing `$__range`, `$__range_s`, or `$__range_ms` are not time-split (as the comment notes, splitting them produces wrong results because `$__range` should reflect the full request range, not a 1-day chunk). If `applyTemplateVariables` interpolates or transforms the expression before `querySupportsSplitting` runs, or if `runShardSplitQuery` has already called `applyTemplateVariables` (line 52 of `shardQuerySplitting.ts`) and then calls `runSplitQuery` (line 163 of `shardQuerySplitting.ts`), `applyTemplateVariables` is executed twice on the same query.
2. Calling `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` in both `runShardSplitQuery` and `runSplitQuery` (and potentially again inside `datasource.runQuery` / `super.query`) applies `request.filters` (ad-hoc filters) multiple times to `query.expr`, injecting duplicate label matchers into the LogQL selector.
